text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
CORN SALES - The Commodity Credit Corp said it bought a total of 85,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow corn for donation to North Korea. The shipment period was slated for August 1-September 10.
- South Korea's Korea Corn Processing Industry Association bought a total of 84,500 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn from Continental Grain through a closed tender.
WHEAT SALES - U.S. exporters sold 200,000 tonnes of soft red winter wheat to Egypt during 1997/98 year, USDA said.

WHEAT SALES - Jordan overnight bought a total of 100,000 tonnes U.S. hard red winter wheat slated for last-half August and last-half September delivery, U.S. exporters said. The wheat was bought in two 50,000 tonne lots.
- The CCC said it bought 6,360 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat for donation to Tunisia. The shipment period was slated for August 10-August 31.
SOYMEAL SALE - A South Korean buyers group, known as the BigFeed Mills, bought 30,000 tonnes of Brazilian soymeal at $277.50 a tonne C&F, officials of the buyers group said.

CORN/SOY TENDERS - Egypt has cancelled a tender for 30,000 tonnes of corn after a government decree was issued requiring proof that grain imports were not genetically altered. It also cancelled a tender for 30,000 tonnes of soybeans because it had received only one offer, making price comparison impossible.

- Taiwan is expected to tender for up to 128,000 tonnes of corn and 138,000 tonnes of soybeans this week if prices on the CBOT dip, traders said. "Buyers are all waiting to finish their September and October supplies," a grains trader said.

RICE AND CORN BLEND TENDER - CCC was seeking on July 24 a total of 10,000 tonnes of U.S. milled rice in bulk and 5,000 tonnes of corn-soy blend in 25 kg bags for donation to North Korea. The corn blend was slated for August 25 delivery but the rice delivery was amended to August 25 to Sept 10.
Soymeal Tender - CCC was seeking up to 7,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean meal in bulk for donation to Nicaragua. The shipemtn was set for August 10-30. Results were due July 24.
WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd have jointly invited tenders to buy 22,500 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat on Wednesday, traders said.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC was seeking up to 3,530 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat on July 30 for donation to Honduras. The shipment period was set for Aug 15-Sept 5.
- The CCC was seeking up to 4,100 tonnes of U.S. Hard Red Winter wheat on July 29 for donation to Bosnia. Shipment period was slated for Aug 15-Sept 5.
- The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender Thursday for 99,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat in three 33,000-tonne shipments, traders said.
- Pakistan on July 28 will be seeking a total of 500,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for August 11-Sept 10 shipment.

VEGOIL TENDER - El Salvador said it was seeking about 4,000 to 5,000 tonnes prime bleachable summer yellow (PBSY) cottonseed oil in bulk and about 750 to 1,250 tonnes sunflowerseed oil under the PL-480, Title I export program, its U.S. export agent said. Offers are to be received by July 29 and remain valid until July 30. The shipment dates for both commodities were slated for September 10-25.

RICE TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.

- The CCC said it was seeking on July 22 a total of 1,780 tonnes U.S. long grain rice for donation to Burkina Faso. The shipment period was due for August 21 to September 5. Results were due on July 24.
MARKET TALK - Chinese buyers were very interested in new crop U.S. soybeans and were likely making enquiries in the market.

... The United States will give Pakistan a $20 million wheat import credit under an agreement signed in Islamabad on Wednesday, a Pakistan government statement said. The credit had been extended by the Commodity Credit Corporation of the U.S. Department of Agriculture under Washington's PL-480 programme.
... China imported 840,000 tonnes of wheat in the first half of the year, down by 82.9 percent from the same period of 1996, the China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday, quoting customs figures.
... Algeria may have bought some milling wheat from Canada but details were lacking, European grain traders said on Wednesday. There was no official confirmation of a deal.

Earlier European grain traders said Algeria was expected to cancel or delay a tender for the purchase of 75,000 tonnes of optional-origin soft wheat for September because of a sharp rise in world prices.
